data.title: Keyframe
data.tagline: The state points you specify in an animation; the browser interpolates animatable properties between specified points
data.learningOutcome: Given a piece of animation code, you can point out which state points it specifies.
data.description: CSS @keyframes lets you specify styles at points such as 0%, 50%, and 100%. The browser calculates values between points for interpolable properties; looping requires a separate animation-iteration-count setting such as infinite, because keyframes do not loop by themselves.

learning.assumes: You have seen looping animations on pages, or AI implementing animation with @keyframes.
learning.outcome: Given a piece of animation code, you can point out which state points it specifies.

distinctions.label: Transition
distinctions.explanation: A transition commonly animates a start and end state after a state change; @keyframes can specify multiple points, while repeat count is set by animation properties such as animation-iteration-count.

distinctions.label: Easing
distinctions.explanation: Easing decides the rhythm curve of the middle; keyframes decide which state points exist. They work together but are not the same.

explanation.title: A transition has only two states
explanation.text: From initial to target state, triggered by hover or click; it plays once and stops.

explanation.title: Keyframes can specify many states
explanation.text: Specify points at 0%, 50%, and 100%; set animation-iteration-count separately if it should loop.

explanation.title: Read the code for state points
explanation.text: Percentages inside @keyframes are the specified points; the browser interpolates between them for animatable properties, while other properties may switch discretely.

data.boundary: Keyframes decide which states exist; easing decides how the middle plays out. The same rotation with different easing curves feels completely different in speed.

lessonPractice.title: A loading icon should rotate in an infinite loop. Which approach fits better?

options.label: Use keyframes: specify 0% and 100% states and set infinite looping
options.feedback: Correct. Looping playback needs keyframes; a transition plays once on a state change and does not loop by itself.

options.label: Use a transition; it will keep rotating when the page refreshes
options.feedback: A transition is triggered by state changes and plays once; it does not loop automatically.

options.label: Swap many images rapidly to simulate rotation
options.feedback: Frame-by-frame images are costly and choppy; a rotation is expressed with keyframes.

data.agentPrompt: Make the loading icon rotate in a loop: use @keyframes for its states and set animation-iteration-count: infinite. Also respect the system's reduced-motion preference; confirm the icon's movement changes when that setting is on.
